Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Ireland's reply. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Stephen Doheny and Andy Balbirnie open up for Ireland. Nathan Smith will start with the new ball. Let's go...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

New Zealand continued to dominate - Coming out to bat on Day 2, the Blackcaps completely shut the door on any hopes of an Irish fightback. Tom Blundell stepped on the gas. He unfortunately fell on 186 runs. Not to be outdone, his partner Dean Foxcroft played an incredibly composed knock on his Test debut, seamlessly converting his overnight 38 into a near miss as he got out on 98 in his debut Test. It will not be easy for the Irish side to overcome this total but they have the got the batting to do it and the backing of the home crowd as well.

The turning point - But Test match cricket is a game of fine margins, and Ireland will look back at the afternoon session with immense regret. Rachin Ravindra was given a massive life on 56 when skipper Andrew Balbirnie spilled a crucial catch at second slip. Ravindra made the hosts pay dearly, smashing a brilliant 121, as part of a massive 217-run partnership with Tom Blundell. Though part-timer Harry Tector finally broke the stand in the evening session, the damage to the Irish spirit was already heavily done.

Ireland started well on Day 1 - Day 1 kicked off in style for the hosts when Mark Adair cleaned up Tom Latham for a duck, followed shortly by Devon Conway for just 4. When debutant Liam McCarthy claimed the massive wicket of Kane Williamson for 36 and Adair removed Daryl Mitchell for 1, New Zealand were absolutely reeling at 86/4.

The declaration - With Foxcroft missing out on a ton in his debut Test, and the scoreboard reading 490 for 8, the Blackcaps finally declared their first innings closed. New Zealand’s mission now completely shifts to the bowling department as they look to bundle Ireland out cheaply. Because this is not a five-day Test match, they will be hunting for a first-innings lead of at least 150 runs to enforce the follow-on and force the hosts to bat back-to-back.

OUT! TAKEN! Oh, Dean Foxcroft was just two runs away from his debut century in Test cricket, but what an inning it was from the 28-year-old. McBrine pitches it fuller and around middle. Foxcroft gets down on one knee to sweep it, but it hits the upper part of the bat. The ball lobs toward short fine leg, where Thomas Mayes takes a sitter. New Zealand have declared their inning on 490 for 8.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the action to begin on Day 2. Tom Blundell and Dean Foxcroft are ready to resume their innings. Thomas Mayes will be bowling the first over on Day 2. Mark Adair has not taken the field for Ireland because of some niggle.

NZ batter Tom Blundell is up for a chat - Tom Blundell says that he is very pleased with how he and Rachin Ravindra worked together to build a strong partnership after the team fell to 86 for 4. Tom noted that the opposing team bowled exceptionally well with the new ball on a challenging wicket that made scoring difficult and required constant focus. Additionally, Blundell adds that he enjoyed batting alongside debutant Dean Foxcroft.

PITCH REPORT ON DAY 2 - Katey Martin is pitchside. Katey mentions that a few green patches have dried up and that will give the bowlers a bit more if they hit the right areas. Katey adds that this will generally be the best day to bat on, as the ball will come nicely onto the bat and the deck will show a lot more wear and tear going ahead.

What to expect today? The equation is simple for both teams as we head into the morning session. For New Zealand, Blundell and Foxcroft will look to bat Ireland out of the game and push past the 500-mark. For Ireland, the new ball is just two overs old, and skipper Andrew Balbirnie will be desperate for early wickets to wrap up the tail. Grab your coffee, settle in, because the first hour promises to be absolute gold!

The Kiwis fought back - But Test cricket is all about resilience, and New Zealand found it in abundance. Rachin Ravindra and Tom Blundell stitched together a massive, game-changing 217-run partnership. Ravindra rode his luck after being dropped once to smash a commanding 121 before part-timer Harry Tector finally got him. Meanwhile, Blundell played an absolute masterclass, finishing the day unbeaten on a stellar 142. Alongside him is debutant Dean Foxcroft, looking solid on 38, pushing the Kiwis to a commanding 361/5.

The Irish started well yesterday - Day 1 belonged to the storylines. Ireland won the toss, opted to bowl, and Mark Adair gave them a dream start by removing Tom Latham for a duck on just the second ball of the match. Devon Conway fell shortly after, and the debutant Liam McCarthy trapped the legendary Kane Williamson for 36. New Zealand were absolutely reeling at 86/4. Adair was the star with the ball, finishing the day with brilliant figures of 3/66.

Welcome to Day 2! Welcome back to our coverage of this fascinating, one-off Test match. After a gripping opening day, the players are warming up, the pitch looks pristine, and we are all set for another action-packed day of traditional red-ball cricket.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

See you tomorrow - That brings an end to all the exciting action from Day 1. The visitors will resume their innings tomorrow at a strong score of 361 for 5. Make sure to tune back in for the start of Day 2 on 28th May 2026 at 10 am GMT. Cheers for now!

Rachin Ravindra of NZ is up for a chat - Rachin says that it felt nice to play here in Ireland in front of an amazing crowd. Rachin adds that Ireland were excellent to begin with, as they lost quick wickets at the start, but they were lucky to recover from that. Rachin Ravindra adds that the wicket got better as the day went on, and he is happy with how things ended. Rachin also reckons that Dean Foxcroft has looked brilliant on his debut as well and he concludes by saying that the crowd is great here and everyone loves this game.

Ireland finally broke the stand - Ireland finally got the breakthrough late in the day when Harry Tector dismissed Ravindra, breaking the epic stand. Adair was the star with the ball, picking up three wickets, but the damage was already done. Blundell remained absolutely immovable, finding a reliable partner in Dean Foxcroft. Together, they added an unbeaten 58 runs before Stumps. Blundell walked off to a standing ovation on 142 not out, with Foxcroft on 38 not out, locking in a dominant position for the Kiwis.

Blundell and Ravindra stitched a massive stand - Enter Tom Blundell. What followed was an absolute masterclass in batting from Blundell and Ravindra. The duo weathered the storm and then launched a sensational counter-attack, putting on a marathon 217 runs together. Both batters raised their bats for spectacular centuries. They played beautifully under the afternoon sun and stayed unbeaten for the entire second session.

Kiwis stumbled further to 86/4 - The session continued with a tense battle. The legendary Kane Williamson tried to steady the ship with Ravindra, but he fell just as things looked stable, leaving the tourists in deep trouble at 85/3. Just a run later, Daryl Mitchell was caught out for a solitary run. At 86/4, New Zealand stared down the barrel of a cheap dismissal. Ireland was on top of the world, but that proved to be their last celebration for a very long time.

Adair fired early for Ireland - Irish skipper Andy Balbirnie won the toss and bowled first under grey skies, and his bowlers delivered early on. Mark Adair was absolutely lethal, finding a sharp opening delivery to send Kiwi captain Tom Latham walking back for a duck. With the ball swinging around, Ireland struck again quickly, leaving New Zealand absolutely rattled at 21/2. The home crowd buzzed as the top order looked totally helpless against a relentless Irish attack.

Kiwis ruled Day 1 - So, New Zealand have ended the day with a massive 361/5, pulling off an incredible rescue act after a disastrous morning. Tom Blundell was the ultimate hero of the day, standing tall with a majestic, unbeaten 142. Alongside him, a brilliant 217-run partnership with young Rachin Ravindra completely turned the game on its head. Ireland started like a house on fire, but the visitors firmly seized control by the time the bails were lifted.

STUMPS ON DAY 1 - A day that was dominated by New Zealand. Ireland started brilliantly by tearing through New Zealand's top order, but the Kiwis fought back fiercely with a massive partnership to gain the momentum at the end of the Day.

Ireland seeking to have the momentum back - Mark Adair has been Ireland's standout performer with three wickets to his name, but few could have anticipated such a fruitless afternoon session for the Irish, particularly after the remarkable momentum they had built, snaring four wickets in the first two hours of play. It will be interesting to see how the bowlers will shape themselves to get their momentum back into the game. Join us at 3.30 pm GMT to witness the action in the last session of Day 1!

Resilience of Rachin and Tom - It didn't take long to recognise that Ravindra and Blundell had emerged from Lunch as a transformed pair. Rachin was first to announce his intent, stroking his way to a sixth Test half-century and visibly growing in confidence with every run. The longer he spent at the crease, the clearer his decision-making became, knowing precisely when to play his shots and when to leave well alone. The same evolution was unfolding at the other end for Blundell. Tom had looked tentative early on, particularly against the short-pitched delivery, which had him shuffling and uncertain, but as his feet found rhythm and his eye sharpened, those poor deliveries started being dispatched to the fence with authority and conviction.

TEA ON DAY 1 - New Zealand resumed after Lunch at 104 for 4, with Rachin Ravindra well set on 45 and Tom Blundell on 10, the pair tasked with rebuilding after a chaotic morning session that saw Ireland draw first blood emphatically. This is the first-ever Test between the two sides, and Ireland came out in the afternoon with the same intent and discipline that had served them so well in the opening session. New Zealand were pegged back at 91 for 4 moments before the Lunch break during the first session,  before Ravindra and Blundell dug in and began to rebuild with patience.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back after the Lunch break! The umpires are striding toward the center of the park, and the Irish players are taking their respective fielding positions. Tom Blundell and Rachin Ravindra resume their inning. Ravindra is just five runs away from his sixth half-century in Test cricket. Rachin stood firm - Despite the quick double-blow, Rachin Ravindra stood firm and found an able partner in Tom Blundell. The duo absorbed the pressure well and ensured there were no further setbacks before the break. Thanks to their resilience, New Zealand managed to cross the 100-run mark, ending the opening session at 104/4. Ireland clearly took the honors in this session, and the game hangs beautifully poised. Can the hosts dominate the second session as well? Or will the Kiwis fight back? Join us at 1.10 pm GMT post the Lunch Break to find out...

The recovery from the Kiwis - With the visitors in deep trouble, Kane Williamson and Rachin Ravindra joined hands to steady the ship. The duo showed immense composure and stitched together a crucial 64-run partnership for the third wicket. Just when New Zealand looked to be recovering, Liam McCarthy stepped up for Ireland. He broke the dangerous stand by taking the wicket of Williamson, and Adair again followed it up quickly by dismissing Daryl Mitchell, leaving the Kiwis reeling at 84/4.

A session that belonged to Ireland - Ireland made a dream start to this 4-day Test match. After opting to bowl first, their bowlers came out firing on all cylinders. Spearheading the attack, Mark Adair struck gold in the very first over, dismissing Kiwi skipper Tom Latham for a duck. Adair didn't stop there. He soon removed Devon Conway for just 4 runs, leaving the New Zealand opening pair shattered early on.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for this historic Test to get underway. The umpires have made their way out in the middle followed by the players of Ireland. The opening pair for New Zealand is out as well with Devon Conway and Tom Latham walking out with the bat for NZ. Mark Adair will take the new ball for Ireland.

The teams take the field for the pre-match ceremonies as the national anthems prepare to play. New Zealand's anthem sounds first, followed immediately by Ireland's anthem to wrap up the pre-game formalities.

PITCH REPORT ON DAY 1 - Isobel Joyce is pitchside and she says the weather is absolutely incredible today with temperatures hovering comfortably in the mid-20s, which means the 22-yard strip is a really good surface for cricket. Joyce notes that it feels nice and firm and the conditions are pretty even all the way around. Looking closely at the surface, Joyce points out that there is virtually no movement or structural cracks to worry about, and while there are a couple of very minor imperfections. Joyce does not expect them to affect how the ball behaves and she adds that the track offers much better, truer carry than is usually seen at this venue, which she calls a fantastic sign for this time of year.

The skipper of New Zealand - Tom Latham expresses happiness after getting his wish to bat first on a dry, high-quality surface boosted by a week of great weather. Since the NZ team last played a Test match in Tasmania, Latham notes that finding their rhythm quickly is their main goal before the series against England. Tom informs that Dean Foxcroft is making his debut as the team opts for a four-man pace attack.

The skipper of Ireland - Andrew Balbirnie acknowledges the honor of playing Test cricket against world-class teams and says that while Ireland have played good cricket in past matches, they must now focus on playing well for longer stretches. Balbirnie informs about the team changes by highlighting that families are present to watch their three debutants, Reuben Wilson, Liam McCarthy, and Thomas Mayes, who lead a three-man pace attack.
New Zealand (Playing XI) - Tom Latham (C), Devon Conway, Kane Williamson, Rachin Ravindra, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Blundell (WK), Dean Foxcroft, Nathan Smith, Zakary Foulkes, Blair Tickner and Ben Sears.
Ireland (Playing XI) - Andy Balbirnie (C), Stephen Doheny, Cade Carmichael, Harry Tector, Curtis Campher, Lorcan Tucker (WK), Mark Adair, Andy McBrine, Thomas Mayes, Reuben Wilson and Liam McCarthy.
TOSS ​​- Ireland have won the coin flip and they have elected to BOWL first.

An exciting battle ahead - This unique match sets up a classic story of New Zealand's seasoned expertise against a depleted but fiercely proud Irish squad. It acts as a direct, real-world test to see if four-day cricket can still deliver the late-game drama, tension, and strategy of a five-day match. This special encounter promises to give fans a truly compelling narrative. It beautifully balances intense, hard-fought international competition with a live experiment that could change the very structure and future of Test cricket forever.

Brave new faces meet tough times - The home team faces an uphill battle as they step onto the field to meet one of the best teams in the world. Ireland is dealing with a severe wave of sudden injuries that has forced senior professionals like Paul Stirling out of action. Despite these massive setbacks, captain Andy Balbirnie leads a highly determined and hopeful side that includes several exciting, uncapped players ready to make their names known. To survive the bowling attack of New Zealand, Ireland will have to rely heavily on the steady bats of Harry Tector and Lorcan Tucker to anchor their innings and fight for runs.

Black Caps prep for the English summer - New Zealand enters this historic match under the calm leadership of captain Tom Latham. The team views this unique game as the absolute perfect warm-up opportunity before they head off for their major, highly anticipated Test series against England. The deeply experienced Kiwi squad features world-class batting stars like Kane Williamson and welcomes back terrifyingly fast bowlers like Kyle Jamieson. A few of their regular players are away due to lucrative franchise commitments. Even so, the powerful Black Caps are incredibly eager to find their rhythm, adjust to the red ball, and dominate the pitch in this format.

A shorter Test for a bold new era - Hello and welcome to all the fans of this beautiful game. The historic first Test match between Ireland and New Zealand at the Civil Service Cricket Club in Belfast is a monumental event for global cricket. This match is a crucial four-day experiment backed by the International Cricket Council. The main goal is to see if shortening the traditional five-day format can save time, cut costs, and make the game more exciting for modern fans. For the hosts, this rare four-day fixture is a deeply proud but highly challenging milestone. It marks only the 13th Test match Ireland has played in the game's longest and most respected format since they first earned their official Test status back in 2017.
